entries.difference: A NUL (U+0000) or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate in a finance record's `title`, sent as a JSON body's `\u0000` or `\ud800` escape (legacy-fixtures/cfml/api.cfm:24-32 merges a JSON body into the params), passes the fixture's title checks, and the create and edit bind it as `cf_sql_nvarchar` (legacy-fixtures/cfml/modules/finance.cfc:61-79,85-104,205-241, binding at 237), so legacy stores it and answers 200. PostgreSQL text holds neither. A NUL fails the statement with SQLSTATE 22021, which finance answers with the legacy-shaped 400 `invalidParameters`, writing nothing (services/finance/src/legacy/envelope.ts:177-179; platform/src/service-kit/create-service.ts:375-385; platform/src/legacy-compat/errors.ts:33). node-postgres sends parameters as UTF-8, which turns the surrogate into U+FFFD, so the target stores and answers `\uFFFD` (`\ud800x` reads back `\uFFFDx` where legacy answers `?x`). entries.difference: Legacy binds every user and address text column as `cf_sql_varchar` or `cf_sql_longvarchar` (core/mura/user/userDAO.cfc:300-355 create, 404-500 update with `company` at 439, 749-808 address update and create with `city` at 757), and its application datasource sets no Unicode string option (core/appcfc/applicationSettings.cfm:496-507), so ACF's SQL Server driver sends the values in the database code page, Windows-1252 under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, although the columns are nvarchar (core/setup/db/mssql.sql:444-464 with `city` at 451, 467-505 with `Company` at 476). Each UTF-16 code unit outside that code page is stored as `?`: on the oracle, `cUsers.updateAddress` stored the city `Zürich 日本 ✓` as `Zürich ?? ?` and Edit Profile stored the company `Émoji 😀 Co ✓` as `Émoji ?? Co ?`, the emoji's two code units each becoming `?`. people stores person and address text exactly as posted (`insertPerson`, `updatePerson`, `insertAddress` and `updateAddress` in services/people/src/repo/repository.ts) and answers it back. The reverse projector binds nvarchar columns as `NVarChar` (migration/src/reverse/apply-legacy.ts:305-337, nvarchar at 315-319), so a target write reaches legacy as exact Unicode, which legacy pages then show. A later legacy save of the same user or address, such as a withheld `{photo}` or `{extdata}` variant inside a write window, rewrites every text column through the binding above, and the window import sends the substituted values back to people as `legacy-window` writes (migration/src/windows/import.ts:470-488), which the projector skips (migration/src/reverse/operations.ts:17-18; platform/src/migration-kit/handlers.ts:86); backfill likewise imports the `?` legacy stores.
entries.reason: The substitution follows from legacy's parameter binding, not from the request, and the target can reproduce it: people is to replace each UTF-16 code unit outside Windows-1252 with `?` before storing, as legacy does, and the reverse projector then writes the same text. Halting these carried writes would take them out of `grp:identity.credential`, so the entry stays open as the record until people applies the substitution, and then closes.

entries.difference: Legacy JSON API feeds of `address` and `user` read rows or columns people does not hold in cases the request decides. An address feed is a `beanFeed` over the site's `tuseraddresses` rows whatever their owner's type (core/mura/user/addressBean.cfc:79; core/mura/bean/beanFeed.cfc:978-979, through core/mura/client/api/json/v1/jsonApiUtility.cfc:2542-2918), so it lists group addresses, which are identity's `user_address` rows (opt2/table-ownership.json). A user feed's `sort` or `orderby` list becomes the `ORDER BY` of `userGateway.getAdvancedSearch`, each item without a table part prefixed `tusers.` (jsonApiUtility.cfc:2955-3071; core/mura/user/userGateway.cfc:567-571), so an item may name a `tusers` column of identity's account, credential or login state other than `username` (`Password`, `PasswordCreated`, `LastLogin`, `Type`, `Admin`, `S2`, `Perm`, `InActive`, `isPublic`, `SiteID`, `remoteID`, `tablist`), a column of `tfiles`, strategies-content's photo join (userGateway.cfc:312), or a column of a table a param's prefix joins (userGateway.cfc:316-333). people answers every address `findAll` and `findQuery`, an address `findMany` naming an id it holds no address for (`addressFeedRefused`), and a user feed ordered by such an item (`applyFeedProps`) with the legacy-shaped 503 (services/people/src/routes/legacy-api.ts).
entries.reason: Equivalence is impossible for these cases, which order or list another owner's rows and columns in one SQL Server statement, so the address and user feed keys stay `legacy` in every cut-over version, and people answers the cases with the legacy-shaped 503. EX-PEOPLE-FEED-ORDER records the user feed orders people refuses although it holds their columns.

entries.difference: Legacy orders a user feed by any `sort` or `orderby` list `setFeedProps` builds, each item without a table part prefixed `tusers.` (core/mura/client/api/json/v1/jsonApiUtility.cfc:2955-3071; core/mura/user/userGateway.cfc:567-571). Three orders over columns people holds are refused with the legacy-shaped 503 (`applyFeedProps` and `addUserParam`, services/people/src/routes/legacy-api.ts): a list of more than one item, such as `sort=lname,fname`; one item naming a person column outside userGateway's built-in sort options `fname`, `lname`, `username`, `company`, `lastupdate`, `created` and `email` (userGateway.cfc:181), such as `sort=jobtitle`; and a findQuery `orderby` param, such as `?lname=Huel&orderby=fname`, which people refuses as the feed's `orderby` setter that `addParam` calls (core/mura/bean/beanFeed.cfc:316-319; jsonApiUtility.cfc:2867-2888) although `setFeedProps` then makes it the order exactly as `sort` (jsonApiUtility.cfc:2905,2961-2967,3071), so legacy answers it ordered by `tusers.fname`.
